note: The cases here need no database: they exercise the decision rules, the participant resolution and the SLA clock, which are the parts §IX.6.3 calls mechanisms. The persistence mechanisms — the conditional UPDATE and the seq under lock — are proved against a real database in tests/workflow_persistence_test.php and tests/workflow_timers_test.php.

cases.title: approve then approve again: the second call is refused and the first decision is unchanged
approve then reject is the same refusal — a decided step is immutable whatever the second decision says
cases.note: SmartPRS 2 re-fires transfer orders and increment letters on re-approval, and its decide() writes remarks unconditionally so a blank re-decide erases the prior reason.

cases.title: quorum at n−1, n and n+1 approvals
parallel_all: a rejection decides the node whichever order the decisions arrive in
at breach−1s nothing escalates; at breach+1s exactly one escalation
and an automatic decision on a timer that fired long after its due instant is WITHHELD
cases.note: R-IX-066. A scheduler outage followed by a catch-up sweep must never silently approve a backlog.

cases.title: the requester holding the approver role is excluded, and the trace names the prohibition
cases.subject: u-priya

cases.title: withdrawal is terminal on a task: any later decision is refused
cases.note: `cancelled` is an INSTANCE state; the terminal task state a requester reaches is `withdrawn`. The corpus said the wrong word and TaskState refused it, which is the closed vocabulary of §IX.4 doing its job — there is no string that is almost a state.

cases.title: two decisions from two connections in two open transactions: exactly one succeeds, the loser gets the decision that stands, exactly one transition row
cases.note: R-IX-045 names this test and names what it must assert. It needs two real connections — one handle deciding twice tests the status column, not the race — so it reports NOT RUN rather than PASS when there is no database.

cases.title: every transition and every refused attempt is in the audit ledger, with actor, timestamp, decision and comment
cases.note: R-IX-105/106/107. The transition ledger and the audit ledger were unconnected: workflow code contained no reference to audit at all. R-IX-107's refused attempts are the half SmartPRS 2 has nothing of — a 403 that writes nothing cannot say who tried.

upstream_refusals.reason: self-approval: the requester is the assignee

cases.title: at, below and above each threshold: ₹49,999.99 to the manager, ₹50,000.00 to the director, and the amendment re-routes
cases.note: R-IX-077: integer minor units, `from` inclusive and `to` exclusive. ₹50,000.00 belongs to exactly one band, and which one is the difference between a manager and a director approving it. SmartPRS 2 compares loan instalments as floats and its SchemeController carries explicit 0.005 epsilons — the code acknowledging its own comparisons are unreliable.

probes.note: a credit note is a real amount, and the unbounded lower band admits it rather than stranding the instance

cases.title: a gap in the bands is a refusal naming the unroutable amount, not a silent fall-through to the last band
cases.note: W08 makes this impossible at publish, so reaching it is a platform bug. It is asserted anyway, because the alternative to refusing is an instance that strands at the node holding the money.

cases.title: a float boundary is refused outright rather than compared
cases.note: R-IX-077. Not 'floats are discouraged': a band boundary that is not an integer never reaches a comparison.

cases.title: an ACTIVE delegation moves the task to the delegate, and the trace names the window it is in force for
the same delegation one day after it ends does nothing — the approver keeps their own work
cases.note: This state could not be expressed at all until delegations carried dates. A delegation raised for a fortnight's leave routed approvals for ever, which is how a queue ends up with somebody who left in March.

cases.title: and on its last day it still applies — `effective_to` is inclusive, because the last day of leave is a day of leave
a chain: A delegates to B, who is out of office with C as backup, so the work lands on C
cases.note: Following one hop and stopping assigns the task to somebody the system already knows is away.

cases.title: a CIRCULAR delegation is refused, naming the loop, and that candidate is excluded rather than resolved arbitrarily
cases.note: A → B → A has no terminal delegate. Taking the first hop hands the task to the person the delegation existed to route around — on half the runs.

cases.title: but only that candidate: a node with another eligible approver still routes
a node that forbids delegation keeps the original approver
cases.note: `delegation_allowed` has been written by the publisher since the workflow payload landed and nothing read it, so a node declaring that its approval may not be delegated was delegating it anyway.

cases.title: R-IX-036 identity 3: whoever holds the work under a delegation from the requester cannot approve it — but only while that delegation is in force
and once it has expired the former delegate is an approver again — an expired delegation is not a permanent taint
a returned task keeps its decision, its actor and its reason, and the resubmission is a new row pointing at it
cases.note: SmartPRS 2 returns a request by writing over the same row — the status goes back to pending and the remark is replaced, so the fact that a manager once returned it, and why, is gone. The reason somebody was asked to fix their claim is exactly what the next approver needs to see.
cases.return_reason: the dates overlap an approved leave

cases.title: an instance mid-flight on v1 completes on v1 while a new instance starts on v2 — and the pin is what the definition is READ through
cases.note: `workflow_instances.config_version_id` existed since the workflow migration and nothing read it, so this was a property of a column rather than of the platform. SmartPRS 2 reads its approval steps from the current configuration on every request, so editing a chain silently rewrites every request already in flight.

cases.title: five maker-checker shapes through ONE engine, and zero approval code outside the workflow namespace
cases.note: SmartPRS 2 has an approval implementation per module, which is why a fix to the leave one never reaches the loan one. The structural half states how many files it actually read, because '0 offenders out of 0 files' is the vacuous version of this check. Note that parallel_all completes as 'joined' and parallel_any as 'first_completed' rather than 'approved': the node's outcome is what the NODE did, and collapsing both into 'approved' is how a join and a race stop being distinguishable in the history.

shapes.label: parallel-all: one outstanding is still pending
parallel-any: the first approval decides it
return-for-edit is an outcome of the same engine
